name: The positive integers. Also called the natural numbers, the whole numbers or the counting numbers, but these terms are ambiguous
note: The base case: d = 1 everywhere, so k = spf(a - 1) and the weight sheet is the sieve of Eratosthenes. The level class is the single line L = 1 (a - 1 prime): 9,592 = pi(99,999) terms here. The ties k = L are a - 1 = p^2: 65 = pi(316).

name: Numbers that are not squares (or, the nonsquares)
note: Non-squares: gaps of 1, and 2 across each square. The plane is the naturals' almost unchanged (9.65 % level against 9.59 %); the gap-2 terms add a short line at L = 2.

name: The prime numbers
note: weight A117078, level A117563, jump A001223, l(n) A118534. Every weight and every level is odd. A prime > 3 is the lesser of a twin pair iff k = 3. Below 10^8 only 2, 3 and 7 fail to decompose.

name: Lower Wythoff sequence (a Beatty sequence): a(n) = floor(n*phi), where phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2 = A001622
note: floor(n phi), a Beatty sequence. The gaps are 1 and 2 only, in the Fibonacci-word pattern, so k is the least divisor of a - d above 1 or 2, as for the naturals and the odd numbers. The level share, 12.20 %, falls between theirs.

name: Triangular numbers: a(n) = binomial(n+1,2) = n*(n+1)/2 = 0 + 1 + 2 + ... + n
note: d = n + 1 and l = (n + 1)(n - 2)/2 = d(n - 2)/2, so l <= d^2 always and L/k < 1/2: every term is level-classified and the cloud stops a factor of two short of the diagonal.

name: The squares: a(n) = n^2
note: d = 2n + 1 and l = (n - 1)^2 - 2 < d^2, so every decomposable term is forced level (100 %). For a ~ c n^2 in general l/d^2 -> 1/(4c), so every quadratic with c > 1/4 ends up entirely level (A002620, c = 1/4, sits on the edge); the nine polynomial-type sequences here differ only in their ray structure.

name: Tetrahedral (or triangular pyramidal) numbers: a(n) = C(n+2,3) = n*(n+1)*(n+2)/6
note: d = (n + 1)(n + 2)/2 grows like n^2 while l grows like n^3/6, so l/d^2 -> 0: every decomposable term is forced level (100 %), and the line L = 1 is thin (329 terms).

name: Pentagonal numbers: a(n) = n*(3*n-1)/2
note: d = 3n + 1 against l = (3n^2 - 7n - 2)/2 < d^2: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %).

name: Square pyramidal numbers: a(n) = 0^2 + 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2 = n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)/6
note: d = (n + 1)^2 against l ~ n^3/3, so l/d^2 -> 0: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %).

name: Hexagonal numbers: a(n) = n*(2*n-1)
note: d = 4n + 1 against l = 2n^2 - 5n - 1 < d^2: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %).

name: The cubes: a(n) = n^3
note: d = 3n^2 + 3n + 1 against l ~ n^3, so l/d^2 -> 0: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %). The line L = 2 is slightly fuller than L = 1 (7,847 against 7,814 terms).

name: Lucky numbers
note: A sieve of the same shape as Eratosthenes, with the same density x / log x. As for the primes, every term is odd and every gap even, so l is odd and every weight is odd. The level share is 32.31 %, against 23.00 % for the primes over a comparable range (a up to 1.43e6 and 1.30e6).

name: Flavius Josephus's sieve: Start with the natural numbers; at the k-th sieving step, remove every (k+1)-st term of the sequence remaining after the (k-1)-st sieving step; iterate
note: count(x) = 2 sqrt(x/pi), so a(n) ~ pi n^2/4 and the gap outgrows sqrt(l): l <= d^2 on 77 % of terms, and 96.6 % of the sequence is level-classified. It is the spread of the gap, not its mean, that populates the weight class.

name: Powers of primes. Alternatively, 1 and the prime powers (p^k, p prime, k >= 1)
note: Prime powers, with 1: the primes plus a sparse set of higher powers. The plane is the primes' plane almost exactly (22.97 % level against 23.00 %).

name: Squares of primes
note: a = p^2 and d = q^2 - p^2 >= 4p + 4, so l < p^2 < d^2: every decomposable term is forced level (100 %). a decomposes iff q^2 < 1.5 p^2. That fails only for p = 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 23; Nagura (a prime in [x, 6x/5] for x >= 25) rules out any other.

name: Semiprimes (or biprimes): products of two primes
note: Omega(n) = 2. The gaps stay small (1 to 47 here) and l/d^2 is large, so only 5 terms are forced level. The level share, 15.71 %, lies between the naturals' and the primes'. The line L = 1 (l prime) carries 61 % of the level class.

name: Lesser of twin primes
note: Past 5 every term is 5 mod 6, so d = 0 and l = 5 (mod 6). No square is 5 mod 6, so k = L can never happen: zero ties, by proof rather than by count. l is prime to 6, so every weight is odd and not a multiple of 3. The level share is 47.77 %.

name: Numbers that are the sum of 2 squares
note: n = x^2 + y^2: every prime 3 mod 4 divides n to an even power. Starts at a(1) = 0. Density ~ 0.764 x / sqrt(log x) (Landau-Ramanujan). The gaps stay below 35 here and the level share is 15.95 %.

name: Numbers not divisible by 3
note: The gaps alternate 1, 2 and 3 divides l at every term. Since d <= 2, the forced divisor 3 is always eligible, so k is 2 or 3 at every decomposable term (24,999 and 74,999 of them) and the cloud collapses to two vertical lines. Only a = 4, 5 and 8 are level-classified: the most weight-dominated sequence in the atlas.

name: Powerful numbers, definition (1): if a prime p divides n then p^2 must also divide n (also called squareful, square full, square-full or 2-powerful numbers)
note: p | n implies p^2 | n; each term is a^2 b^3 with b squarefree, uniquely. count(x) ~ (zeta(3/2)/zeta(3)) sqrt(x) = 2.17 sqrt(x), so the sequence thins out like a quadratic one. The jump outgrows sqrt(l) on 42.07 % of terms (forced level) and 71.90 % are level-classified.

name: Sorting numbers: maximal number of comparisons for sorting n elements by binary insertion
note: d = ceil(log2 n) exactly, constant on dyadic blocks. l/d^2 grows without bound so the level-forcing criterion never fires: 68 % weight. The gap sets a left wall - no weight column below k = d can exist.

name: Sum of totient function: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} phi(k), cf. A000010
note: a(n) = sum of phi(k) for k <= n, from a(0) = 0; a ~ 3n^2/pi^2 and d = phi(n+1) <= n, so the sequence is nearly quadratic. l <= d^2 on 45.98 % of terms and 87.35 % are level-classified. For n >= 2 both a and d are even, so 2 | l. Since a > 3d on every decomposable term, l/2 > d, so k <= l/2 and L >= 2: the line L = 1 is empty.

name: Palindromes in base 10
note: Starts at a(1) = 0. Only 13 distinct gaps below 10^12, all of the form 10^j or 11*10^j (plus the single value 2). The plane is self-similar with period 2 in the digit length; the level share oscillates 60/94 % with its parity.

name: Primes of the form 4*k + 3
note: Every term is 3 mod 4 and every gap 0 mod 4, so l = 3 (mod 4). No square is 3 mod 4: zero ties, by proof. l is odd, so every weight is odd. The level share, 28.16 %, is above the primes' 23.00 %.

name: Oblong (or promic, pronic, or heteromecic) numbers: a(n) = n*(n+1)
note: n(n + 1) = 2 T(n): d = 2n + 2 and l = (n - 2)(n + 1) < d^2, forced level (100 %). l is even and l/2 > d for n > 6, so L >= 2: the line L = 1 holds only a = 30 and 42.

name: Quarter-squares: a(n) = floor(n/2)*ceiling(n/2). Equivalently, a(n) = floor(n^2/4)
note: floor(n^2/4), from a(1) = 0 (a(0) = a(1) = 0). The gap takes each value twice and l <= d^2 throughout: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %).

name: The composite numbers: numbers n of the form x*y for x > 1 and y > 1
note: Composites: gaps of 1, and 2 across each prime. The naturals' plane, thinned: 10.58 % level against 9.59 %.

name: Ulam numbers: a(1) = 1; a(2) = 2; for n>2, a(n) = least number > a(n-1) which is a unique sum of two distinct earlier terms
note: Rigid: gap 2 alone carries 37 % of the terms. The signal at alpha = 2.5714475 acts on the classification only through the gap - across phase bins mean gap and level share correlate at r = 0.9957.

name: Self numbers or Colombian numbers (numbers that are not of the form m + sum of digits of m for any m)
note: Self numbers: not of the form m + digitsum(m). They come in runs spaced 11 apart - gap 11 on 89.8 % of the terms - broken at decade boundaries. The level share is 24.93 %.

name: Fibbinary numbers: if n = F(i1) + F(i2) + ... + F(ik) is the Zeckendorf representation of n (i.e., write n in Fibonacci number system) then a(n) = 2^(i1 - 2) + 2^(i2 - 2) + ... + 2^(ik - 2). Also numbers whose binary representation contains no two adjacent 1's
note: No two adjacent 1 bits in binary. The decomposition fails 24 times, each where the sequence jumps to the next power of two (a(n+1) >= 1.5 a(n)). Gap 1 carries 62 % of the terms and the level share is 10.35 %.

name: Skip 1, take 1, skip 2, take 2, skip 3, take 3, etc
note: Closed form { m^2+j : 1 <= j <= m }. Interior terms (d = 1) follow the naturals rule; block openers m^2+1 give a tie exactly when m is prime; every block closer satisfies l <= d^2 and is level.

name: a(0) = 1, a(n) = sum of digits of all previous terms
note: a(n) = a(n-1) + digitsum(a(n-1)), so 9 divides l at every term. Above a = 800 every level term lies on a line L in 9Z (a level term off 9Z needs l <= 3d^2, impossible past a = 10^4), and Lemma 3 (L <= d) caps the lines at the gap: with d <= 50 in this range only L = 9, 18, 27, 36 occur. The 12 level terms off 9Z are all below 800.

name: Abundant numbers (sum of divisors of m exceeds 2m)
note: sigma(n) > 2n. 99.2 % of these terms are even (the first odd one is 945), and so is l on 99.2 % of decomposable terms: the level class sits on even L, and the line L = 1 holds only 32 terms.

name: Squarefree numbers: numbers that are not divisible by a square greater than 1
note: Squarefree numbers, density 6/pi^2. Gaps of 1 to 7; the plane is close to the naturals' (10.72 % level) and L = 1 carries almost all of the level class.

name: Practical numbers: positive integers m such that every k <= sigma(m) is a sum of distinct divisors of m. Also called panarithmic numbers
note: Practical numbers. Every term > 2 is divisible by 4 or 6, so a and d are even and 2 | l at every decomposable term: the line L = 1 holds only 2 terms and the level class sits on L = 4, 6, 8, ... The level share is 17.50 %.

name: Triangular numbers together with squares (excluding 0)
note: The union of two sequences that are 100 % level-classified is not: merging triangular numbers and squares shrinks the gaps below sqrt(l) on 58.6 % of terms, and 16.2 % turn weight. No ties occur.

name: Niven (or Harshad, or harshad) numbers: numbers that are divisible by the sum of their digits
note: n divisible by its digit sum. Density by digit sum is 9:3:1 according to gcd(s,9), but that structure does not reach the plane: the weight fence is flat and the level share varies only between 11 and 24 %.

name: The odd numbers: a(n) = 2*n + 1
note: d = 2 and l = a - 2 is odd, so the divisor 2 is never available and k = spf(a - 2). The level class is exactly {a : a - 2 prime}, all on L = 1: 17,982 = pi(199,997) - 1 terms here. The ties are a - 2 = p^2, 85 = pi(447) - 1. Removing the divisor 2 nearly doubles the level share against the naturals: 17.98 % against 9.59 %.

name: The nonnegative even numbers: a(n) = 2n
note: d = 2 and l = a - 2 = 2m. The level class is exactly {a : m an odd prime}, all on the line L = 2, plus a = 6 (L = 1) and a = 10: the naturals' level line, moved from L = 1 to L = 2 (9.59 % level, the same share).

name: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} floor(n/k); also Sum_{k=1..n} d(k), where d = number of divisors (A000005); also number of solutions to x*y = z with 1 <= x,y,z <= n
alias: Sum of d(k) for k <= n
note: Sum of d(k) for k <= n, ~ n log n; the gap is d(n+1) (1 to 128 here). The level share, 23.41 %, is close to the primes' 23.00 %.

name: Numbers k such that floor(sqrt(k)) divides k
alias: Numbers k with floor(sqrt k) | k
note: Blocks {m^2, m^2 + m, m^2 + 2m} with gaps m, m, 1. The first two terms of each block have l <= d^2 and are forced level - exactly two thirds of the sequence (66.67 %). The third, with d = 1 and l = (m+1)^2 - 2, never a square, behaves like a natural number: no ties.

name: Greater of twin primes
note: Past 5, every term is 1 mod 6, so l = 1 (mod 6): squares are possible and 29 ties occur, where the lesser twins (l = 5 mod 6) have none. The level share, 46.93 %, is close to the lesser twins' 47.77 %.

name: Squarefree semiprimes: Numbers that are the product of two distinct primes
note: Products of two distinct primes. The plane is the semiprimes' almost exactly (15.72 % level against 15.71 %).

name: The binary numbers (or binary words, or binary vectors, or binary expansion of n): numbers written in base 2
note: n in binary, read in decimal. The gap is (8*10^j + 1)/9 = 1, 9, 89, 889, ... where j counts the trailing 1 bits of n: sixteen values here, and the plane splits into clean diagonal lines. Capped at 65,535 terms, since a(65,536) = 10^16 passes 2^53.

name: Sum of the first n primes
note: Sum of the first n primes: a ~ n^2 log n / 2 and d = p(n+1), so l/d^2 -> 0 like 1/(2 log n): every decomposable term is forced level (100 %).

name: a(n) = prime(n) + 1
note: p + 1. The gap is the prime gap and l = p + 1 - g is even, so 2 | l; l/2 > d on all but two terms (a = 3, 6), and the primes' level line L = 1 moves to L = 2, which holds 43 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are not powers of primes p^k (k >= 0); complement of A000961
note: Numbers with at least two distinct prime factors. Gaps of 1 to 4; the plane is close to the naturals' (10.59 % level).

name: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} k*floor(n/k); also Sum_{k=1..n} sigma(k) where sigma(n) = sum of divisors of n (A000203)
alias: Sum of sigma(k) for k <= n
note: Sum of sigma(k) for k <= n: a ~ pi^2 n^2/12 = 0.822 n^2 and d = sigma(n+1) > n: every decomposable term is forced level (100 %).

name: Number of prime divisors (counted with multiplicity) is odd; Liouville function lambda(n) (A008836) is negative
note: Omega(n) odd (Liouville lambda = -1). Gaps of 1 to 16; the level share is 12.82 %.

name: Numbers without 0 in the decimal expansion, colloquial 'zeroless numbers'
note: No digit 0. Gap 1 almost everywhere, with jumps 2, 12, 112, ... across the zeros; the plane is the naturals' (10.54 % level).

name: Odious numbers: numbers with an odd number of 1's in their binary expansion
note: Numbers with an odd number of 1 bits. Gaps are 1, 2 and 3, each on a third of the terms. The level share is 11.01 %, next to the evil numbers' 11.39 %, with 86 ties each. 84 % of the level class sits on L = 1 and the rest on L = 3.

name: Evil numbers: nonnegative integers with an even number of 1's in their binary expansion
note: Numbers with an even number of 1 bits, the complement of the odious numbers. Gaps are 1, 2 and 3, each on a third of the terms. The level share is 11.39 % against 11.01 % for the odious numbers. The level class sits on L = 1 (76 %) and L = 3.

name: Heptagonal numbers (or 7-gonal numbers): n*(5*n-3)/2
note: n(5n - 3)/2. For a ~ c n^2, l/d^2 -> 1/(4c); here c = 5/2, so l <= d^2 and every decomposable term is forced level (100 %), as for the squares and pentagonal numbers.

name: Octagonal numbers: n*(3*n-2). Also called star numbers
note: n(3n - 2), a ~ 3 n^2 and d = 6n + 1: l < d^2, so every decomposable term is forced level (100 %). The lines L = 1 and L = 2 are about equally full (6.1 % and 6.0 % of the level class).

name: Centered square numbers: a(n) = 2*n*(n+1)+1. Sums of two consecutive squares. Also, consider all Pythagorean triples (X, Y, Z=Y+1) ordered by increasing Z; then sequence gives Z values
note: 2n(n + 1) + 1 = n^2 + (n + 1)^2. d = 4(n + 1) and a ~ 2 n^2 < d^2: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %). Every l is odd and the fullest line is L = 3 (10.9 %), ahead of L = 1 (8.4 %).

name: Hex (or centered hexagonal) numbers: 3*n*(n+1)+1 (crystal ball sequence for hexagonal lattice)
note: 3n(n + 1) + 1, the hex numbers. d = 6(n + 1) and a ~ 3 n^2 < d^2: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %). L = 1 holds 13.8 % of the class, then L = 5 (6.9 %).

name: Centered triangular numbers: a(n) = 3*n*(n-1)/2 + 1
note: 3n(n - 1)/2 + 1. d = 3n and a ~ 1.5 n^2 < d^2: forced level at every decomposable term (100 %).

name: Central polygonal numbers (the Lazy Caterer's sequence): n(n+1)/2 + 1; or, maximal number of pieces formed when slicing a pancake with n cuts
note: n(n + 1)/2 + 1, the triangular numbers moved up by one. With c = 1/2 > 1/4 the terms are all forced level (100 %), like the triangular numbers, but the line L = 1 is much thinner: 1,342 terms against 2,642.

name: a(n) = n^2 + 1
note: n^2 + 1. d = 2n + 1 and l = n^2 - 2n < d^2: every decomposable term is forced level (100 %). The line L = 1 (l prime) is thin: 1,225 terms.

name: Generalized pentagonal numbers: m*(3*m - 1)/2, m = 0, +-1, +-2, +-3, ...
note: m(3m - 1)/2 for m = 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, ... Two quadratics interleaved: the gaps alternate j and 2j + 1. With a ~ 1.5 j^2 the gap j leaves l > d^2 while the gap 2j + 1 forces level, so exactly half the terms (49,999) are forced level. The other half is split, and the level share ends at 77.61 %.

name: Pentagonal pyramidal numbers: a(n) = n^2*(n+1)/2
note: n^2 (n + 1)/2, the pentagonal pyramidal numbers. d grows like n^2 while l grows like n^3, so l/d^2 -> 0: every decomposable term is forced level (100 %).

name: Octahedral numbers: a(n) = n*(2*n^2 + 1)/3
note: n(2n^2 + 1)/3. A cubic sequence: l/d^2 -> 0 and every decomposable term is forced level (100 %). L = 1 holds 9.4 % of the terms and L = 2 half as many.

name: Upper Wythoff sequence (a Beatty sequence): a(n) = floor(n*phi^2), where phi = (1+sqrt(5))/2
note: floor(n phi^2) = floor(n phi) + n, the complement of the lower Wythoff sequence. The gaps are 2 and 3 only (38 % and 62 %). The level share, 15.38 %, is above the lower sequence's 12.20 %; the level class lies on the lines L = 1, 2 and 3.

name: A Beatty sequence: a(n) = floor(n*sqrt(2))
note: floor(n sqrt 2), a Beatty sequence with gaps 1 and 2 only. The level share is 11.37 %, on the lines L = 1 (82 %) and L = 2.

name: Beatty sequence for sqrt(3); complement of A054406
note: floor(n sqrt 3), a Beatty sequence with gaps 1 and 2 only (27 % and 73 %). The level share is 12.69 %, on the lines L = 1 (72 %) and L = 2.

name: Pythagorean primes: primes of the form 4*k + 1
note: Every term is 1 mod 4 and every gap 0 mod 4, so l = 1 (mod 4) and ties are possible (23 here), where the primes 3 mod 4 have none. The level share, 27.95 %, is close to theirs (28.16 %). The fullest level line is L = 3.

name: Primes of the form 6m + 1
note: Every term is 1 mod 6 and every gap 0 mod 6, so l = 1 (mod 6). The level share, 35.24 %, is almost the primes 5 mod 6's 35.16 %, but they have no ties and these have 48.

name: Primes of the form 6k-1
note: Every term is 5 mod 6 and every gap 0 mod 6, so l = 5 (mod 6). No square is 5 mod 6: zero ties, by proof. The level share is 35.16 %, and half the level class sits on L = 1.

name: Sophie Germain primes p: 2p+1 is also prime
note: p with 2p + 1 prime. Past 3 every term is 5 mod 6, so l = 5 (mod 6) and no tie can occur, as for the lesser twin primes. The level share, 47.25 %, is close to theirs (47.77 %).

name: Safe primes p: (p-1)/2 is also prime
note: p with (p - 1)/2 prime. Past 7 every term is 11 mod 12 and every gap 0 mod 12, so l = 3 (mod 4): no square, no tie. The level share, 51.96 %, is the highest among the prime subsequences here.

name: Prime-indexed primes: primes with prime subscripts
note: prime(prime(n)). The gaps are larger and more varied than the primes' (662 distinct values here), and the level share rises to 43.29 %, against 23.00 % for the primes.

name: Single (or isolated or non-twin) primes: Primes p such that neither p-2 nor p+2 is prime
note: Primes p with neither p - 2 nor p + 2 prime. Level share 26.11 %, a little above the primes' 23.00 %; L = 1 and L = 3 carry 60 % of the level class.

name: Twin primes
note: Primes in a twin pair, both members. Past 5 every l is 3 mod 6: after a lesser twin d = 2 and l = p - 2; after a greater twin d = 4 (mod 6). So 3 | l, and the line L = 1 holds only 6 terms. All but 68 level terms sit on odd multiples of 3 (L = 3, 9, 15, ...). The level share is 19.67 %.

name: Primes p such that p + 4 is also prime
note: p with p + 4 prime. Past 3 every term is 1 mod 6, so l = 1 (mod 6) and ties can occur (31 here). The level share, 46.77 %, is close to the lesser twins' 47.77 %.

name: Primes p such that p + 6 is also prime. (Lesser of a pair of sexy primes.)
note: p with p + 6 prime. The terms mix 1 and 5 mod 6, and the level share, 34.58 %, lies between the primes' and the twin primes'.

name: Emirps (primes whose reversal is a different prime)
note: Primes whose decimal reversal is a different prime. No emirp begins with 2, 4, 5, 6 or 8 (its reversal would be even or a multiple of 5), so whole blocks are skipped. The largest gap is 3,000,162, and 12 terms fail to decompose. The level share is 31.54 %.

name: a(n) = prime(n) - 1
note: p - 1. Past 2 every term and every gap is even, so 2 | l. The primes' level line L = 1 moves to L = 2, which holds 45 % of the level class (compare p + 1). There are no ties, and the line L = 1 holds a single term.

name: Numbers that are the product of exactly three (not necessarily distinct) primes
note: Omega(n) = 3. The gaps stay between 1 and 34 here. The level share is 15.79 %, beside the semiprimes' 15.71 %, and L = 1 carries 64 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are products of 4 primes
note: Omega(n) = 4. The level share is 16.89 %. The lines L = 1 and L = 2 are nearly equal (36 % and 33 % of the level class); 65 % of the terms are even.

name: Sphenic numbers: products of 3 distinct primes
note: Products of three distinct primes. The level share is 17.04 %, against 15.72 % for the squarefree semiprimes.

name: Numbers that are not squarefree. Numbers that are divisible by a square greater than 1. The complement of A005117
note: Numbers divisible by a square > 1. Only four gaps occur here, 1 to 4. The level share is 13.03 %, spread over L = 1, 2, 4 and 3.

name: Weak numbers (i.e., not powerful (1)): there is a prime p where p|n is true but p^2|n is not true
note: Numbers that are not powerful (some prime divides them exactly once). Gap 1 on 99.4 % of the terms. The plane is the naturals' almost unchanged: 9.62 % level against 9.59 %.

name: Deficient numbers: numbers k such that sigma(k) < 2k
note: sigma(n) < 2n. Gaps 1 and 2, with 38 gaps of 3. Every level-classified term lies on L = 1, and the level share, 7.79 %, is the lowest here after the numbers not divisible by 3.

name: Loeschian numbers: numbers of the form x^2 + xy + y^2; norms of vectors in A2 lattice
note: x^2 + xy + y^2: every prime 2 mod 3 divides n to an even power. Starts at a(1) = 0. The level share, 24.23 %, is well above the sums of two squares' 15.95 %.

name: Numbers of the form x^2 + 2*y^2
note: x^2 + 2y^2: every prime 5 or 7 mod 8 divides n to an even power. Starts at a(1) = 0. Level share 14.91 %, with half the level class on L = 1.

name: Numbers that are the sum of 2 nonzero squares
note: x^2 + y^2 with x, y >= 1. The plane is almost exactly that of all sums of two squares (15.97 % level against 15.95 %).

name: Sums of three squares: numbers of the form x^2 + y^2 + z^2
note: Sums of three squares, the numbers not of the form 4^a(8b + 7) (Legendre). Density 5/6 and gaps of 1 to 3. The level share is 8.54 %, 99 % of it on L = 1.

name: Numbers that are the sum of 4 but no fewer nonzero squares
note: 4^a(8b + 7), the complement of the sums of three squares. Half the gaps are 8. The level share is 23.71 %, with L = 1 holding half the level class.

name: Numbers not divisible by 2, 3 or 5
note: Numbers prime to 2, 3 and 5. The gaps are 2, 4 and 6, repeating with period 8. The level class lies on only three lines: L = 3 (43 %), L = 1 and L = 5.

name: Numbers congruent to 1 or 5 mod 6
note: 6m + 1 and 6m + 5, with gaps 4 and 2. Then 3 | l at every term, so after a gap of 2 the weight is 3. After a gap of 4, a term is level essentially when l/3 is prime. The level class is the naturals' level line moved to L = 3 (9.59 % level).

name: a(n) = 3*n
note: 3n: d = 3 and l = 3(n - 1). The level class is essentially {3n : n - 1 prime}, all on the line L = 3, like the even numbers' line L = 2. The level share is 9.60 %.

name: Odd nonprimes
note: 1 and the odd composites. Gaps 2, 4, 6 and 8. The level share, 21.01 %, is above the odd numbers' 17.98 %; 97 % of the level class is on L = 1.

name: Happy numbers: numbers whose trajectory under iteration of sum of squares of digits map (see A003132) includes 1
note: The digit-square-sum iteration reaches 1. The gaps are irregular (58 distinct values up to 73) and the level share is 19.71 %.

name: Numbers that contain a digit 0
note: Numbers with at least one digit 0; starts at a(1) = 0. Only the gaps 1 and 10 occur here, and the level class lies on the two lines L = 1 and L = 10. The level share is 8.76 %.

name: Numbers that contain odd digits only
note: Every decimal digit odd. The gaps are 2, 12, 112, 1112, ... (80 % are 2). The level share is 17.40 %.

name: Numbers in base 3
note: n in base 3, read in decimal. The gaps are 1, 8, 78, 778, ..., one per count of trailing 2 digits, so the plane splits into clean lines. 21 terms fail to decompose, and the level share is 10.70 %.

name: Numbers whose base-3 representation contains no 2
note: No digit 2 in base 3: the integers of the Cantor set, and the greedy sequence with no three terms in arithmetic progression. The gaps are (3^j + 1)/2 = 1, 2, 5, 14, ... Level share 14.75 %, and no ties.

name: Moser-de Bruijn sequence: sums of distinct powers of 4
note: Sums of distinct powers of 4: binary n read in base 4. The gaps are (2*4^j + 1)/3 = 1, 3, 11, 43, ... The level share is 13.96 %; L = 1 and L = 2 hold 73 % of the level class. No ties.

name: Numbers whose binary representation ends in an even number of zeros
note: n with an even number of trailing 0 bits (the 2-adic valuation is even). Gaps 1 and 2. Every level term lies on L = 1, there are no ties, and the level share is 13.88 %.

name: Binary palindromes: numbers whose binary expansion is palindromic
note: Binary palindromes; starts at a(1) = 0. There are about sqrt(x) of them up to x, so the sequence thins out like a quadratic. The gap outgrows sqrt(l) on 35 % of terms (forced level), and 88.40 % are level-classified.

name: a(n) = n*(n+3)/2
note: n(n+3)/2, the triangular numbers minus one, shifted: T(n+1) - 1. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = n*(n+2) = (n+1)^2 - 1
note: n(n+2) = (n+1)^2 - 1. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = 2*n^2
note: 2n^2. Every term and every gap is even, so 2 | l, and the line L = 1 holds only 2 terms. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Odd squares: a(n) = (2n+1)^2. Also centered octagonal numbers
note: (2n+1)^2. d = 8(n+1) and l = (2n+1)^2 - 8(n+1) is odd. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Generalized octagonal numbers: k*(3*k-2), k=0, +- 1, +- 2, +-3, ..
note: m(3m - 2) for m = 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, ... Two quadratics interleaved: the gaps alternate 4j and 2j + 1 while a ~ 3j^2, so both leave l <= d^2. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered pentagonal numbers: (5n^2+5n+2)/2; crystal ball sequence for 3.3.3.4.4. planar net
note: (5n^2 + 5n + 2)/2, the centered pentagonal numbers. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered octahedral numbers (crystal ball sequence for cubic lattice)
note: (2n+1)(2n^2+2n+3)/3, the centered octahedral numbers. A cubic sequence. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered cube numbers: n^3 + (n+1)^3
note: n^3 + (n+1)^3, the centered cube numbers. A cubic sequence. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Stella octangula numbers: a(n) = n*(2*n^2 - 1)
note: n(2n^2 - 1), the stella octangula numbers. A cubic sequence. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = 1^2 + 3^2 + 5^2 + 7^2 + ... + (2*n-1)^2 = n*(4*n^2 - 1)/3
alias: Sums of the first n odd squares
note: 1^2 + 3^2 + ... + (2n-1)^2 = n(2n-1)(2n+1)/3. A cubic sequence. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Hexagonal pyramidal numbers, or greengrocer's numbers
note: n(n+1)(4n-1)/6, the hexagonal pyramidal numbers. A cubic sequence. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Cake numbers: maximal number of pieces resulting from n planar cuts through a cube (or cake): C(n+1,3) + n + 1
note: (n^3 + 5n + 6)/6, the most pieces from n plane cuts of a cube. A cubic sequence with d = T(n) + 1. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = n*(n^2 + 1)/2
note: n(n^2 + 1)/2, the magic constant of an n x n magic square. A cubic sequence. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Second hexagonal numbers: a(n) = n*(2*n + 1)
note: n(2n+1), the second hexagonal numbers. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Second pentagonal numbers: a(n) = n*(3*n + 1)/2
note: n(3n+1)/2, the second pentagonal numbers. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Triangular matchstick numbers: a(n) = 3*n*(n+1)/2
note: 3n(n+1)/2 = 3 T(n). 3 | a and 3 | d, so 3 | l, and the line L = 1 holds only 3 terms. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = floor(n^2/3)
note: floor(n^2/3), from a(1) = 0 (a(0) = a(1) = 0). Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = floor(n^2/2)
note: floor(n^2/2), from a(1) = 0 (a(0) = a(1) = 0). Terms and gaps are even past the start, so the line L = 1 holds 2 terms. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = floor(n^(3/2))
note: floor(n^(3/2)). The gap grows like sqrt(n) while l grows like n^(3/2), so l/d^2 grows like sqrt(n) and almost no term is forced level. The level share is 46.64 %.

name: Primes of form 8n+1, that is, primes congruent to 1 mod 8
note: Primes 1 mod 8. Every gap is 0 mod 8, so l = 1 (mod 8) and ties are possible. The level share is 33.30 %.

name: Primes == 3 (mod 8)
note: Primes 3 mod 8. Every gap is 0 mod 8, so l = 3 (mod 8); no square is 3 mod 4, so there are no ties, by proof. The level share is 33.29 %.

name: Primes of the form 8k + 5
note: Primes 5 mod 8. Every gap is 0 mod 8, so l = 5 (mod 8); no square is 5 mod 8, so there are no ties, by proof. The level share is 33.29 %.

name: Primes of the form 8*k+7, that is, primes congruent to -1 mod 8
note: Primes 7 mod 8. Every gap is 0 mod 8, so l = 7 (mod 8); no square is 3 mod 4, so there are no ties, by proof. The level share is 33.13 %.

name: Primes of the form 10*n+1
note: Primes ending in 1. Every gap is a multiple of 10, so l ends in 1 as well. The level share is 37.20 %.

name: Primes of form 10n+3
note: Primes ending in 3. Every gap is a multiple of 10, so l ends in 3; no square ends in 3, so there are no ties, by proof. The level share is 37.28 %.

name: Primes of form 10n+7
note: Primes ending in 7. Every gap is a multiple of 10, so l ends in 7; no square ends in 7, so there are no ties, by proof. The level share is 37.30 %.

name: Primes of form 10*k + 9
note: Primes ending in 9. Every gap is a multiple of 10, so l ends in 9 and ties are possible. The level share is 37.29 %.

name: Balanced primes (of order one): primes which are the average of the previous prime and the following prime
note: Primes that are the mean of their two neighbours. They are sparse (the 100,000th is 56,206,697), and the gaps are large and varied. The level share is 52.42 %; 1.0 % of terms are forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Strong primes: prime(k) > (prime(k-1) + prime(k+1))/2
note: Primes above the mean of their two neighbours. The level share is 29.38 %.

name: Weak primes: prime(n) < (prime(n-1) + prime(n+1))/2
note: Primes below the mean of their two neighbours. The level share is 29.87 %.

name: Primes p such that 2p-1 is also prime
note: Primes p with 2p - 1 prime. The level share is 47.76 %; L = 1 holds 35 % of the level class.

name: Primes p such that (p+1)/2 is prime
note: Primes p with (p + 1)/2 prime. The level share is 52.16 %; L = 1 holds 31 % of the level class.

name: Primes p such that p + 8 is also prime
note: Primes p with p + 8 prime. Past 3 every term is 5 mod 6 (p + 8 must avoid 3), so l = 5 (mod 6): no ties, by proof. The level share is 47.00 %; L = 1 holds 37 % of the level class.

name: Primes followed by a gap of 6, i.e., next prime is p + 6
alias: Lower prime of a gap of 6
note: Primes whose next prime is p + 6. The level share is 36.03 %.

name: Initial members of prime triples (p, p+2, p+6)
note: p with p, p + 2, p + 6 all prime. Past 5 every term is 5 mod 6, so l = 5 (mod 6): no ties, by proof. The level share is 63.42 %; 3.9 % of terms are forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Initial members of prime triples (p, p+4, p+6)
note: p with p, p + 4, p + 6 all prime. Past 7 every term is 1 mod 6. The level share is 66.20 %; 3.8 % of terms are forced level (l <= d^2); L = 1 holds 31 % of the level class.

name: Products of 2 successive primes
note: p(n) p(n+1). d = p(n+1)(p(n+2) - p(n)) is at least 2 p(n+1), so d^2 > a. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = n * prime(n)
note: n p(n). d = n (p(n+1) - p(n)) + p(n+1) > p(n) > n, so d^2 > n p(n) = a. Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = n-th prime + n
note: p(n) + n. The gap is the prime gap plus 1. The level share is 25.35 %; L = 1 holds 31 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are the sum of 2 successive primes
note: p(n) + p(n+1), all even past the first term. l is even, and the line L = 1 holds a single term. The level share is 24.90 %.

name: The primes doubled; even semiprimes
note: 2p. The primes' decomposition doubled: d = 2g and l = 2(p - g), so the primes' level line L = 1 moves to L = 2. 23,004 terms are level-classified, against 22,999 for the primes. The level share is 23.00 %; L = 2 holds 32 % of the level class; there are no ties.

name: a(n) = 3 * prime(n)
note: 3p. The level share is almost the primes' 23.00 %. The level share is 23.02 %; L = 3 holds 32 % of the level class.

name: Numbers which are the product of a prime and the square of a different prime (p^2 * q)
note: p q^2 with distinct primes p, q. The level share is 27.45 %.

name: Products of exactly four distinct primes
note: Products of four distinct primes. The level share is 21.02 %; L = 2 holds 34 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are products of 5 primes (or 5-almost primes, a generalization of semiprimes)
note: Omega(n) = 5. The level share is 17.97 %.

name: Cubefree numbers: numbers that are not divisible by any cube > 1
note: No cube > 1 divides n. Density 1/zeta(3) = 0.83. The level share is 10.16 %; L = 1 holds 99 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are not cubefree. Numbers divisible by a cube greater than 1. Complement of A004709
note: Divisible by a cube > 1. The level share is 14.06 %; L = 8 holds 37 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are divisible by exactly 2 different primes; numbers n with omega(n) = A001221(n) = 2
note: Exactly two distinct prime factors, any exponents. The level share is 13.17 %; L = 1 holds 66 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are divisible by exactly three different primes
note: Exactly three distinct prime factors, any exponents. The level share is 13.55 %; L = 1 holds 60 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are divisible by exactly four different primes
note: Exactly four distinct prime factors, any exponents. The level share is 17.16 %; L = 2 holds 37 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are the product of an even number of distinct primes
note: Squarefree with an even number of prime factors (Moebius mu = 1). The plane is nearly the mu = -1 plane (14.67 % level against 14.60 %). The level share is 14.67 %; L = 1 holds 71 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are the product of an odd number of distinct primes
note: Squarefree with an odd number of prime factors (Moebius mu = -1). The plane is nearly the mu = 1 plane. The level share is 14.60 %; L = 1 holds 71 % of the level class.

name: Numbers with an even number of prime divisors (counted with multiplicity); numbers k such that the Liouville function lambda(k) (A008836) is positive
note: Omega(n) even (Liouville lambda = 1), the complement of the odd-Omega numbers (12.82 % level there). The level share is 12.78 %; L = 1 holds 70 % of the level class.

name: Numbers j such that the average of the divisors of j is an integer: sigma_0(j) divides sigma_1(j). Alternatively, numbers j such that tau(j) (A000005(j)) divides sigma(j) (A000203(j))
note: The mean of the divisors, sigma(n)/d(n), is an integer. The level share is 11.93 %; L = 1 holds 97 % of the level class.

name: Values taken by totient function phi(m) (A000010)
note: Values of Euler's phi. Past 1 every totient is even, so 2 | l and the line L = 1 holds 2 terms. The level share is 12.58 %; L = 4 holds 40 % of the level class.

name: Values not in range of Euler phi function
note: Not a value of Euler's phi: every odd number > 1 and some even ones. Gaps 1 and 2. The level share is 11.10 %; L = 1 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: Numbers in base 4
note: n in base 4, read in decimal. The gaps are 1, 7, 67, 667, ... The level share is 12.65 %; L = 1 holds 59 % of the level class.

name: Numbers in base 5
note: n in base 5, read in decimal. The gaps are 1, 6, 56, 556, ... The level share is 11.07 %; L = 1 holds 63 % of the level class.

name: Numbers in base 6
note: n in base 6, read in decimal. The gaps are 1, 5, 45, 445, ... The level share is 10.58 %; L = 1 holds 90 % of the level class.

name: Numbers with no 0's in base-4 expansion
note: No digit 0 in base 4. The level share is 12.21 %; L = 1 holds 85 % of the level class.

name: Numbers whose ternary expansion contains no 0
note: No digit 0 in base 3: the digits are 1 and 2. After the numbers not divisible by 3 it has the lowest level share in the atlas, and the line L = 1 holds only 9 terms. The level share is 4.86 %; L = 3 holds 53 % of the level class; there are no ties.

name: Numbers that contain a digit 1 in their decimal representation
note: At least one decimal digit 1. Only the gaps 1 to 10 occur. The level share is 11.06 %; L = 1 holds 90 % of the level class.

name: "9ish numbers": decimal representation contains at least one nine
note: At least one decimal digit 9. Only the gaps 1 to 10 occur. The level share is 13.62 %; L = 1 holds 81 % of the level class.

name: Numbers without 1 as a digit
note: No decimal digit 1. Gaps jump across every block with a 1 (the largest here is 100,001). The level share is 9.31 %; L = 1 holds 79 % of the level class.

name: Numbers without 2 as a digit
note: No decimal digit 2. The level share is 10.38 %; L = 1 holds 97 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that contain even digits only
note: Every decimal digit even. The gaps are 2, 12, 112, ..., as for the only-odd-digit numbers. The level share is 11.08 %; L = 2 holds 63 % of the level class.

name: Numbers with digits in nondecreasing order
note: Decimal digits never decrease (0, 1, ..., 9, 11, 12, ...). There are only C(d+9, 9) of them with d digits or fewer, so the terms grow fast: the 100,000th has 11 digits. The level share is 19.84 %; 2.7 % of terms are forced level (l <= d^2); L = 1 holds 43 % of the level class.

name: Numbers with digits in nonincreasing order
note: Decimal digits never increase (0, ..., 9, 10, 11, 20, ...). The level share is 17.19 %; 2.0 % of terms are forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Numbers whose sum of digits is a prime
note: The digit sum is prime. The level share is 10.71 %; L = 3 holds 44 % of the level class.

name: Numbers whose sum of digits is even
note: The digit sum is even. Gaps 1 to 3. The level share is 10.05 %; L = 1 holds 66 % of the level class.

name: Unhappy numbers: numbers having period-8 2-digitized sequences
note: The digit-square-sum iteration never reaches 1 (it falls into the cycle through 4). The level share is 10.38 %; L = 1 holds 92 % of the level class.

name: Non-Niven (or non-Harshad) numbers: numbers which are not a multiple of the sum of their digits
note: Not divisible by the digit sum: the complement of the Harshad numbers. The level share is 8.25 %; L = 1 holds 99 % of the level class.

name: Nonpalindromic numbers
note: Not a decimal palindrome. Gaps 1 and 2 only. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 1 holds 99 % of the level class.

name: Digitally balanced numbers: positive numbers that in base 2 have the same number of 0's as 1's
note: As many 0 bits as 1 bits. The level share is 11.83 %; L = 1 holds 65 % of the level class.

name: Numbers whose binary representation ends in an odd number of zeros
note: An odd number of trailing 0 bits, the complement of A003159. Every term is twice a term of A003159. Both have exactly 13,875 level terms, all on L = 1 there and here almost all on L = 2. The level share is 13.88 %; L = 2 holds 100 % of the level class; there are no ties.

name: Beatty sequence for 1+sqrt(2); a(n) = floor(n*(1+sqrt(2)))
note: floor(n(1 + sqrt 2)), the complement of floor(n(1 + 1/sqrt 2)). Gaps 2 and 3. The level share is 14.92 %; L = 1 holds 60 % of the level class.

name: A Beatty sequence: a(n) = floor(n*(1+1/sqrt(2)))
note: floor(n(1 + 1/sqrt 2)), the complement of floor(n(1 + sqrt 2)). Gaps 1 and 2. The level share is 12.55 %; L = 1 holds 73 % of the level class.

name: A Beatty sequence: a(n) = floor(n*(2 + sqrt(2)))
note: floor(n(2 + sqrt 2)), the complement of floor(n sqrt 2). Gaps 3 and 4. The level share is 17.24 %; L = 1 holds 50 % of the level class.

name: Beatty sequence for sqrt(5)
note: floor(n sqrt 5). Gaps 2 and 3. The level share is 14.41 %; L = 1 holds 62 % of the level class.

name: Beatty sequence for sqrt(6)
note: floor(n sqrt 6). Gaps 2 and 3. The level share is 15.07 %; L = 1 holds 59 % of the level class.

name: Beatty sequence for sqrt(7)
note: floor(n sqrt 7). Gaps 2 and 3. The level share is 15.61 %; L = 1 holds 57 % of the level class.

name: Beatty sequence for sqrt(8)
note: floor(n sqrt 8). Gaps 2 and 3. The level share is 16.01 %; L = 1 holds 54 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are the sum of 2 distinct nonzero squares
alias: Sums of two distinct nonzero squares
note: x^2 + y^2 with 0 < x < y. The plane is that of all sums of two squares (15.98 % level against 15.95 %). The level share is 15.98 %; L = 1 holds 39 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are the sum of three nonzero squares
note: x^2 + y^2 + z^2 with x, y, z >= 1. The level share is 8.56 %; L = 1 holds 99 % of the level class.

name: Numbers that are not the sum of 2 squares
note: Not a sum of two squares: some prime 3 mod 4 divides n to an odd power. The level share is 13.38 %; L = 1 holds 79 % of the level class; there are no ties.

name: Complement of triangular numbers (A000217); also array T(n,k) = ((n+k)^2 + n-k)/2, n, k > 0, read by antidiagonals
note: Not a triangular number. Gaps 1, and 2 across each triangular number. The level share is 9.51 %; L = 1 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: The noncubes: a(n) = n + floor((n + floor(n^(1/3)))^(1/3))
note: Not a cube. Gaps 1, and 2 across each cube: the naturals' plane. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 1 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: Non-Fibonacci numbers
note: Not a Fibonacci number. Gaps 1 and 2: the naturals' plane. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 1 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: Perfect powers: m^k where m > 0 and k >= 2
note: 1 and m^e with e >= 2. About sqrt(x) of them lie below x, so the sequence thins out like the squares, and 97.8 % of terms are forced level. The level share is 99.25 %; 97.8 % of terms are forced level (l <= d^2); there are no ties.

name: Numbers that are not perfect powers
note: Not a perfect power. Gaps 1 to 3: the naturals' plane. The level share is 9.65 %; L = 1 holds 99 % of the level class.

name: Sequence and first differences (A030124) together list all positive numbers exactly once
note: Hofstadter's figure-figure sequence: a(n+1) = a(n) + (the n-th number not in the sequence). a ~ n^2/2 and every term is forced level (100 %). Every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Numbers not divisible by 5
note: Not divisible by 5. Gaps 1 and 2. The level share is 10.38 %; L = 1 holds 85 % of the level class.

name: Multiples of 4
note: 4n: d = 4 and l = 4(n - 1). The level class is essentially {4n : n - 1 an odd prime}, on the line L = 4. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 4 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: Multiples of 5: a(n) = 5 * n
note: 5n: d = 5 and l = 5(n - 1). The level class lies on the line L = 5, as for the multiples of 3 on L = 3. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 5 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: Nonnegative multiples of 6
note: 6n: d = 6 and l = 6(n - 1). The level class lies on the line L = 6. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 6 holds 100 % of the level class; there are no ties.

name: Multiples of 7
note: 7n: d = 7 and l = 7(n - 1). The level class lies on the line L = 7. The level share is 9.60 %; L = 7 holds 100 % of the level class.

name: a(n) = 3*n + 1
note: 3n + 1: d = 3 and l = 3n - 2, prime to 3. The level share is about twice the multiples of 3's (9.60 %). The level share is 19.91 %; L = 1 holds 65 % of the level class.

name: a(n) = 3*n + 2
note: 3n + 2: d = 3 and l = 3n - 1 = 2 (mod 3), never a square: no ties, by proof. The level share is 19.93 %; L = 1 holds 65 % of the level class.

name: a(n) = 4*n + 1
note: 4n + 1: d = 4 and l = 4n - 3 = 1 (mod 4), odd. The level share is 23.15 %; L = 1 holds 73 % of the level class.

name: a(n) = 4*n + 3
note: 4n + 3: d = 4 and l = 4n - 1 = 3 (mod 4), never a square: no ties, by proof. The level share is 23.15 %; L = 1 holds 73 % of the level class.

name: 9-gonal (or enneagonal or nonagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(7*n-5)/2
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 699,994; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 10-gonal (or decagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(4*n-3)
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 799,993; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 11-gonal (or hendecagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(9*n-7)/2
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 899,992; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 12-gonal (or dodecagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(5*n-4)
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 999,991; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 13-gonal (or tridecagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(11*n - 9)/2
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 1,099,990; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 14-gonal (or tetradecagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(6*n-5)
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 1,199,989; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 15-gonal (or pentadecagonal) numbers: n*(13n-11)/2
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 1,299,988; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: 16-gonal (or hexadecagonal) numbers: a(n) = n*(7*n-6)
note: Every gap is different, from 1 to 1,399,987; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered 9-gonal (also known as nonagonal or enneagonal) numbers. Every third triangular number, starting with a(1)=1
note: Every gap is different, from 9 to 900,000; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered 10-gonal numbers
note: Every gap is different, from 10 to 1,000,000; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = (11*n^2 - 11*n + 2)/2
note: Every gap is different, from 11 to 1,100,000; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered 12-gonal numbers, or centered dodecagonal numbers: numbers of the form 6*k*(k-1) + 1
note: Every gap is different, from 12 to 1,200,000; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: Centered heptagonal numbers
note: Every gap is different, from 7 to 700,000; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = (4*n+1)*(4*n+3)
note: Every gap is different, from 32 to 3,200,000; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = 2*n*(2*n+1)
note: Every gap is different, from 6 to 799,998; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = n*(4*n-1)
note: Every gap is different, from 3 to 799,995; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).

name: a(n) = n*(4*n+1)
note: Every gap is different, from 5 to 799,997; every decomposable term is forced level (l <= d^2).
